findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body: Calling `recordIssuedToken` passes the complete live token to `console.log`. In environments that retain or forward console output, log readers can recover reusable credentials and impersonate users. Audit only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted paths
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a request or query parameter, absolute and protocol-relative values now redirect authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site. The previous fixed destination did not permit this. Validate that the destination is an allowed same-origin path before navigation.

findings.title: [P2] Check for own cache values before trimming
findings.body: With a normal object and a prototype-colliding key such as `toString`, `cache[key]` resolves to an inherited function and the new `.trim()` call throws. Confirm the key is an own string-valued property before trimming it.

findings.title: [P2] Validate the return URL before post-login navigation
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` comes from an untrusted redirect parameter, an absolute cross-origin or dangerous-scheme URL makes the authenticated browser navigate to attacker-controlled content instead of the previously fixed `/dashboard`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict return URLs to same-origin paths before navigating
findings.body:
Passing an attacker-controlled absolute URL such as `https://evil.example/login` now redirects users off-site after authentication, enabling trusted-domain phishing and open-redirect abuse.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Never write issued tokens to the audit log
findings.body:
Every call with a bearer or session token passes the raw credential to `console.log`; production console collection, support logs, or browser diagnostics can therefore expose reusable authentication credentials.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Check for own cache values before invoking `trim`
findings.body:
A valid call using a normal empty cache and a prototype-colliding key, such as `cachedName({}, "toString")`, now throws because the inherited function is non-nullish but has no `trim` method. Arbitrary cache keys can therefore cause a runtime failure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every call with a live bearer/session token passes that credential to `console.log`. In environments that retain or forward console output, anyone with log access can recover valid tokens and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` comes from a request or query parameter, an attacker can supply an absolute or protocol-relative external URL and redirect authenticated users to a phishing site. The previous implementation always navigated to a fixed trusted path.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
